statement_record.book: An Ab-category (preadditive category) is a category in which each hom-set A(a,b) is an additive abelian group and composition is bilinear: (g + g') ∘ (f + f') = g∘f + g∘f' + g'∘f + g'∘f'. Examples: Ab, R-Mod, Mod-R.
statement_record.intree: Preadditive: each hom-setoid carries a commutative MONOID (padd, pzero) respecting ≈, with composition distributing over addition on both sides and pzero absorbing composition — deliberately CMon-enrichment, 'Additive inverses are deliberately not demanded' (header). Additive: upgrades homs to abelian groups (pneg, padd_pneg) but additionally packages a zero object and chosen biproducts for every pair.
statement_record.strength_comparison: neither class matches exactly: Preadditive is intree-weaker (commutative monoids, no additive inverses — every Ab-category is an instance, but the class does not capture the group structure); Additive is intree-stronger (it has the abelian-group homs and full bilinearity including negation via compose_pneg_left/right, but demands a zero object and all binary biproducts, which MacLane's Ab-category does not require).

gap: No in-tree class captures exactly MacLane's Ab-category (abelian-group hom-enrichment with bilinear composition and nothing more): the negation upgrade exists only bundled inside Additive together with a zero object and chosen biproducts; an 'Ab-enrichment only' intermediate class (Preadditive + pneg) is absent. The book's motivating examples Ab, R-Mod, Mod-R are also not in-tree as categories (the concrete preadditive witness is CMon, commutative monoids).
